name: goes_back_with_the_full_name
why: Creating a configuration makes the new one ACTIVE. Going back to one from before is therefore the most normal move there is after making a variant, and it is the green to lean the refusals on: without it, «I cannot find that name» would not tell a check that works from one that refuses everything.
_why_the_boolean_is_not_enough: `ShowConfiguration2` answers a boolean, and on a name that does not fit answers `false` and nothing else -- no exception, no message. Here we look at which configuration is active NOW, read from the state of the document, which is a different road from the one the operation took.

expect.why: the second dislodges the first, again without anybody having asked for it

THE HALF THAT COUNTS. That the name answered is «Left» would also be said by an operation that copies the argument and activates nothing: what proves the move is that the state of the document, read elsewhere, says the same thing.

expect._why_false: HERE WE REALLY MOVED: we were coming from «Right». It is the green half of the field, which in the twin `limit_default_is_not_named_default` must answer «true» -- a field that always answers the same thing tells nothing apart.

expect.why: the variants are born as copies: moving between them does not change the part as long as nobody makes them diverge
